Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

complain verb and noun

also complaint, make a complaint, grumble, moan, complain to someone, complain about

classical

Cic. Fam. 3.10.7: quererer tēcum atque expostulārem
Sen. Ep. 56.7: quae nōn audit audīsse sē queritur

queror, querī, questus sum

verb, third conjugation, deponent; with an accusative, dē + ablative, an accusative and infinitive, or quod; to someone, cum aliquō or apud aliquem

complain (of), lament

What one complains of in the accusative (injūriam querī) or with dē; the person complained to with cum or apud. It is also to lament one’s lot, and in poetry of birds’ song (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • querēla (querella), querēlae f. — a complaint

    noun, first declension · classical · Cic. Q. Fr. 3.8.1 (Lewis & Short): epistula plēna querēlārum

    The usual noun; with a genitive of what it is about, querēla temporum, a complaint against the times (Cic. Fam. 2.16.1). After Augustus also a formal accusation (Petronius, the Digest).

  • conqueror, conquerī, conquestus sum — complain at length, pour out one’s complaints

    verb, third conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Plaut. Mil. 125: conqueritur mēcum mulier fortūnās suās

    A fuller, louder complaining than queror.

  • querimōnia, querimōniae f. — a complaint, grievance

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Plaut. Men. 785: neuter ad mē īrētis cum querimōniā

  • expostulō, expostulāre, expostulāvī, expostulātum — complain to someone’s face, remonstrate

    verb, first conjugation; cum aliquō (dē aliquā rē) · also used · classical

    Classically to have it out with someone, cum aliquō expostulāre; later chiefly to demand urgently (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • quotiēns tandem ēdīxī tibi, ut cavērēs, neuter ad mē īrētis cum querimōniā?

    How many times have I told you to make sure that neither of you came to me with a complaint?Plaut. Men. 784–785

  • quererer tēcum atque expostulārem

    I would complain to you and have it out with youCic. Fam. 3.10.7

  • hūc nempe versātur atque illūc, somnum inter aegritūdinēs levem captāns; quae nōn audit audīsse sē queritur

    he tosses this way and that, trying to catch a light sleep between his worries, and complains that he has heard what he doesn’t hearSen. Ep. 56.7

See also alas!, wail, mind, against.
